=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:91-96 (CLASSIFIER_OUTAGE_REASON_RE with re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The regex compiles with `re.DOTALL`, which makes `.` match across newlines in the reason text. A multi-line `PermissionDenied` reason that includes a debug message such as "classifier is unavailable" on a non-classifier denial will be misclassified as a classifier outage. The third alternative (`\b(?:no|without\s+a|did\s+not\s+return\s+a|could\s+not\s+reach\s+a)\s+verdict\b.*\bclassifier\b`) similarly lets a no-verdict phrase elsewhere in a multi-line reason match when `classifier` only appears in a debug line.
  WHY: A real permission denial whose reason embeds classifier debug output (e.g. "Permission denied. (classifier: unavailable to test this rule)") would be excluded from patterns, total, filed-state.json, and filing, and only counted in outage_denials. The plan acknowledges this in Risks & Mitigations, but the DOTALL flag widens the false-positive surface beyond what the plan's wording describes. The simplest mitigation would be to drop `re.DOTALL` and require the no-verdict phrase + classifier to coexist on the same line, or to match a stricter pattern that does not span newlines.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:9 (step 0 — "A `— resume.` stage session reads its mode from the log's `Stage model: … Permission mode: <mode>` line instead") | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Step 0 is described as "Session preflight" and is the first numbered step in the procedure, but a resume stage is told to read its mode from the progress log, which is not read until step 2 ("Pick the mode, read the progress log first, then project context"). The text as written leaves the resume stage with no concrete instruction for when or how to consult the log inside step 0 — the mode is needed before step 0's "Permission mode — Auto mode is required" check can be evaluated, and the fallback `get_session` is gated by "when the log has no such line", which is a step 2 read.
  WHY: A resume stage session without a `Permission mode:` line in the log falls back to `get_session`, which is precisely the call the change set out to remove. Step 0 will issue that call before the log is read in step 2, so the "no self lookup" promise holds only for resume stages that already have a `Permission mode:` line in their log. The change could either move the log read up into step 0 (so the mode is available before any preflight) or make step 0's "permission mode" read an env var (e.g. the same `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID` style slot) when the log is not yet read.
- docs/plans/issue-4750-classifier-outage-get-session-plan.md, agents.md, and CLAUDE.md | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The plan's §Constraints and the agents.md/CLAUDE.md §23.I pointer both enumerate the new identifiers the phase introduces (`CLASSIFIER_OUTAGE_REASON_RE`, `CLASSIFIER_OUTAGE_LABEL`, `is_classifier_outage`, `split_classifier_outages`, `classifier_outage_summary`, and the `outage_denials` summary key). The implementation also introduces a sixth function, `summarize_permission_records`, that is not in that list. The identifier is unique in the module and ships inside the new code path, so it is not a §6 collision, but the plan-and-agents/CLAUDE.md enumeration it leans on (§5, §6, §7 — the same surface that records the agreed-on scope) is now out of date relative to the actual code, and the new function is what enables the single-log-load optimization that the round-1 review asked for. Without the new name in the plan/agents, a future maintainer comparing the implementation against the documented contract cannot tell from those docs whether `summarize_permission_records` was an intentional split or an out-of-scope addition.
  WHY: No runtime defect — the function is correctly used and tests pass. The gap is in the contract surface that the plan, agents.md, and CLAUDE.md are supposed to keep in sync with the code (§7).
- Requirement: Plan §Non-goals and §Constraints state that every `.claude/**` change is made only in the `workflow-templates/.claude/**` twins and copied into `.claude/**` by the supervising session.   Expected change site: `.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py` and `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` should be byte-identical to their `workflow-templates/.claude/**` twins at the conclusion of the PR.

No further gap.
